title: A Summer for the Vow
premise: When Theo Amberdale finds an undelivered letter from her late grandfather hidden in the lighthouse wall — postmarked eleven years ago and addressed to the woman who left Saltmere Bay without saying goodbye — she sets out to deliver it herself. The letter's recipient, Marisol Vane, turns out to be the estranged mother of Callum, the quiet boat restorer renting Theo's cottage, and the truth it carries threatens both families' carefully kept silences about a storm that killed two men and spared one. As Theo and Callum unravel what really happened, she must confront her own guilt over the night she chose to survive instead of warn, forgive the person in the mirror, and admit the heart cannot be trained into stillness. In the end, the letter is finally read aloud from the lighthouse gallery, Marisol comes home, and Theo chooses love over containment as the lamp is lit for another summer.
about_author: Rosalind Ishikawa spent three summers living in a decommissioned lighthouse keeper's cottage on the northern coast, where she collected local storm lore and the letters people never sent. She writes romances about stubborn hearts and salt air from a small studio overlooking a harbor that never quite sleeps.

chapters.title: The Wall Keeps Its Secrets
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. While repairing storm damage to her grandfather's lighthouse cottage, Theo pries loose a brick and finds a sealed, yellowed letter postmarked eleven years ago. She recognizes the handwriting as her grandfather's but not the addressee: M. Vane. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpened by unease, as her tidy, controlled life develops its first crack.

chapters.title: A Stranger in the Cottage
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum, restoring his late father's fishing boat on Theo's property, notices her distraction and offers help sanding the porch she's ignoring. Their banter reveals he arrived in Saltmere Bay only last month, chasing something he won't name. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth; two guarded people circling each other like tides.

chapters.title: What the Postmark Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo interrogates the town archivist and learns Marisol Vane was her grandfather's closest friend — and vanished the week after the drowning storm of eleven years ago. The name makes the old harbormaster go pale. Emotional beat: dread blooming; the past is not past, and the town has been complicit in burying it.

chapters.title: The Name on the Rent Check
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo discovers Callum's emergency contact is listed as 'M. Vane — mother.' Confronting him, she learns he came to Saltmere Bay hunting answers about his mother's disappearance, carrying half a photograph of the lighthouse. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into alliance; their private griefs turn out to share an address.

chapters.title: Eleven Summers of Silence
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum shares his childhood memory of his mother leaving in the night, and Theo reads him the first lines of the letter before stopping, unable to continue. He asks why she can't finish; she lies. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared wounds, shadowed by Theo's growing fear of what the letter will demand of her.

chapters.title: The Storm File
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Digging through her grandfather's logs, Theo reconstructs the night of the storm: two boats out, one warning never radioed, her grandfather ashore with Marisol. A marginal note in his hand — 'She stayed. I let her go' — suggests the letter is a confession. Emotional beat: vertigo; the grandfather she idolized had hands in the tragedy.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Stakes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo and Callum track Marisol to a coastal town two hours south, but find her hospital room empty — discharged days ago, gravely ill, destination unknown. Time is now explicitly running out. On the drive back, almost-kiss in the truck cab, broken by Theo retreating behind her trained heart. Emotional beat: urgency entwined with longing denied.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A nightmare cracks open Theo's buried memory: at seventeen, during a smaller storm, she ignored a distress flare to protect her grandfather's secret, and a deckhand drowned. She has been 'training' her heart ever since to feel nothing. Emotional beat: the novel's dark night of the soul; forgiveness must begin with herself.

chapters.title: Where the Letter Was Always Going
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum finds Marisol at a hospice overlooking the bay — she never left; she'd been watching the lighthouse for years. He brings Theo, and together they climb the gallery as Marisol, frail and forgiving, asks to hear the letter at last. Emotional beat: climax; confession, absolution, and the reading that frees three generations at once.

chapters.title: Lighting the Lamp
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Weeks later, Marisol rests in the keeper's cottage, Callum finishes his father's boat and launches it, and Theo writes the final page of her novel — then burns her old list of rules for the trainable heart. At dusk they light the lamp together, and she kisses him without flinching. Emotional beat: resolution; found family assembled, memory honored, survival finally worth its price.
